title: Synthetic acceptance and rejection tests for the Expedition verifier core
claim: The canonical local verifier core accepts a matching sealed digest, rejects a nonmatching answer, rejects empty normalized input, and rejects an unknown challenge under five public synthetic tests.
why_it_matters: It makes the verifier behavior inspectable without disclosing the sealed Expedition 001 answer and establishes a repeatable precondition for packaging the puzzle.
scope: Synthetic test vectors only. This run does not open Expedition 001, reveal its answer, or establish that its Windows portable build is customer-ready.
method: Run the standard-library unittest suite against a temporary synthetic manifest whose known test answer is independent of XPD-0001. Exercise normalization, match, nonmatch, empty input, and unknown-ID paths.
controls: The positive synthetic vector must match its generated SHA-256 digest; the negative vector must not match; no XPD-0001 answer is stored in the tests.
reproduction: Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Expected result: five tests pass.
limitations: Unit tests establish deterministic core behavior, not desktop usability.
The sealed XPD-0001 acceptance test is performed privately against the packaged candidate before campaign approval.
This is not Liber Primus source evidence or a plaintext claim.
